2610.11140.title: ActiveMedAgent: Cost-Aware Trajectory Learning for Multimodal Medical Diagnosis
2610.11140.paper_summary: Clinical diagnosis is inherently sequential: clinicians escalate from cheap to costly tests only when additional evidence is expected to resolve diagnostic uncertainty. We present ActiveMedAgent, a framework that brings this cost-aware sequential logic to multimodal medical AI. Given a frozen, API-accessed vision-language model, ActiveMedAgent tracks probability distributions over candidate diagnoses and scores each acquisition by its per-step diagnostic utility minus cost. A lightweight MLP controller is then trained offline on these scored trajectories, learning when to request additional evidence and when to commit. Across three commonly used benchmarks, trajectory-based policy learning consistently outperforms both unguided acquisition and full-modality baselines. Notably, we identify an information overload effect. In 175 cases, the agent produces a correct diagnosis with fewer channels while the full-modality baseline fails, showing that learning what to omit can be as important as learning what to acquire.
2610.11140.paper_summary_zh: 臨床診斷本質上是順序性的：臨床醫生只有在預期額外證據能解決診斷不確定性時，才會從便宜的檢測升級到昂貴的檢測。我們提出了 ActiveMedAgent，一個將這種成本意識的順序邏輯引入多模態醫療 AI 的框架。在一個凍結的、可通過 API 訪問的視覺-語言模型下，ActiveMedAgent 追蹤候選診斷的概率分佈，並根據每一步的診斷效用減去成本來評分每次獲取。然後，一個輕量級的 MLP 控制器在這些評分的軌跡上離線訓練，學習何時請求額外證據以及何時做出承諾。在三個常用基準上，基於軌跡的策略學習始終優於無指導獲取和全模態基準。值得注意的是，我們識別出一種信息過載效應。在 175 個案例中，代理在較少的通道下產生了正確的診斷，而全模態基準失敗，顯示出學習省略哪些信息與學習獲取哪些信息同樣重要。
